title: Daily Market Digest: September 20, 2026
subtitle: Markets Closed on Sunday; Review of Friday, September 18, 2026 Session

sections.title: Market Pulse: Friday's Mixed Close Amid Fed Hike and Yield Surge

items.headline: U.S. Equities Closed Mixed on Friday Following Fed Rate Hike; Tech Sector Showed Strength
items.summary: U.S. stock markets ended the week with a mixed performance on Friday, September 18, 2026. The Nasdaq Composite and S&P 500 posted modest gains, driven by strong performance in the technology sector, while the Dow Jones Industrial Average slipped. Investor sentiment was largely shaped by the Federal Reserve's recent interest rate hike and a surge in Treasury yields. Please note, markets are closed today, Sunday, September 20, 2026. This report summarizes the trading session of Friday, September 18, 2026. Not financial advice.

items.headline: MicroStrategy Surges on Bitcoin Rebound
items.summary: Strategy (formerly MicroStrategy) rocketed 16.4% as Bitcoin reclaimed the $80,000 level.

items.headline: Coinbase Jumps on Crypto Rally
items.summary: Coinbase Global climbed 11.7% for the biggest gain among S&P 500 stocks as the crypto complex rallied.

items.headline: SanDisk Rises on S&P 100 Inclusion
items.summary: SanDisk gained 11%, driven by its upcoming inclusion in the S&P 100 and continued strength in memory pricing.

items.headline: Netflix Drops After Downgrade
items.summary: Netflix was hammered, down 4.7%, after Wells Fargo downgraded the stock citing worrying viewer trends and a lack of breakout hits.

items.headline: Qualcomm Slips as Rally Unwinds
items.summary: Qualcomm dropped nearly 6% as its recent rally unwound.

items.headline: General Motors Experiences Decline
items.summary: General Motors fell 5.1% during Friday's trading session.

items.headline: Federal Reserve Hikes Rates for First Time in Three Years
items.summary: The Federal Reserve raised its benchmark interest rate by a quarter point this week to a target range of 3.75% to 4.00%, marking its first hike in three years. Policymakers also signaled the possibility of another rate increase before year-end as inflation remains elevated.

items.headline: 10-Year Treasury Yield Touches 5% Amid Rate Hike Expectations
items.summary: The yield on the 10-year Treasury climbed to 5.00% on Friday, up from 4.94% late Thursday, topping 5% for the first time since 2023. This rise in bond yields reflects market confidence in further Federal Reserve rate hikes to combat inflation.

items.headline: Technology Sector Leads Market Strength on Friday
items.summary: Tech stocks were the main market driver on September 18, with the Nasdaq index, dominated by tech stocks, showing strong performance with gains exceeding 1%. Artificial intelligence, cloud computing, and semiconductor sectors performed particularly well, driven by optimistic earnings expectations.

items.headline: Energy and Financial Sectors Underperform Amid Rate Changes and Oil Fluctuations
items.summary: In contrast to the strong performance of tech stocks, the energy sector fell 1.3%, mainly affected by international oil price fluctuations, while the financial sector declined 0.8%, reflecting market concerns about changes in the interest rate environment.

items.headline: Initial Jobless Claims Fall to Six-Week Low
items.summary: Initial jobless claims for the week ending September 12 fell to 196,000, a decrease of 10,000 from the previous week's unrevised level, demonstrating the labor market is still holding up.

items.headline: U.S. Industrial Production Flat in August
items.summary: U.S. industrial production was unchanged in August, missing expectations after increasing in July. Manufacturing output decreased by 0.3% in August.

items.headline: No Major Earnings Reports on Friday, M&T Bank to Release Q3 Later
items.summary: No major U.S. earnings reports were scheduled or released on Friday, September 18, 2026. However, M&T Bank Corporation ($MTB) announced it would release its third-quarter 2026 earnings results before the market opens on Friday, October 16, 2026.
